Review pass 43. bd-01KZXW5MFZGEXVJ3CMKMGBGFZX closed and verified.

You took the decoupled form, and expressed it better than I did:

  expected_standard_deviations <- c(null = 0.0058 * sqrt(120), signal = 0.0119 * sqrt(120))
  expected_standard_errors    <- expected_standard_deviations / sqrt(replications)

Keeping the constants as "reference SE times sqrt(120)" rather than precomputed numbers means the provenance is visible in the expression - a reader can see where 0.0635 would have come from instead of having to trust it.

HEADROOM RECOVERED. Expected SE at 64 replications is now null 0.00794, signal 0.01629. Against the SEs I measured independently at 64 (null 0.00860, signal 0.01418):

  ratio observed/expected : null 1.083   signal 0.870   (gate 1.50)
  headroom                : null 39%     signal 72%
  before                  : null  1%     signal 26%

The variance gate is no longer one seed from spurious failure, and the bias gate is back to a genuine 4 sigma rather than the effective 2.7 it had drifted to. 32 expectations, 0 failures.
